Why does my cat rub its face on walls and furniture?
When a cat pushes the cheek, forehead, chin, or side of the face against an object and slides past it, the behavior is commonly described as facial rubbing, bunting, or head bunting.
Cats have scent-producing glands around several areas of the face.
When the face contacts a person or surface, chemical information can be deposited there.
Humans usually cannot smell this feline message.
That is probably fortunate.
If feline facial scent were as obvious to the human nose as perfume, your pants, sofa corners, and door frames might have a very complicated fragrance profile by now.
For cats, however, scent is an important layer of environmental information.
A familiar home does not simply look familiar.
It also smells familiar.
Facial rubbing, scratching, and other scent-related behaviors help cats interact with that chemical environment.
So when your cat casually walks through the living room and rubs a cheek along the sofa corner, you are usually watching a very ordinary part of cat life.
Why do cats love corners so much?
Watch where your cat rubs and you may notice a pattern.
Door frames.
Chair legs.
Cabinet corners.
The corner of the couch.
Your ankle.
Cats seem to have a suspicious level of enthusiasm for anything that sticks out slightly.
There does not need to be a complicated explanation.
A corner gives the cat a convenient surface to place the side of the face against while continuing to move forward.
The cat can press the cheek into the edge, slide the head past it, and continue walking.
From the human side, it looks almost as if the cat is tapping a transit card while moving around the house.
Beep.
Sofa approved.
Beep.
Door frame approved.
Beep.
Human ankle also apparently approved.
If your cat has rubbed the same furniture corner every day for years and otherwise behaves normally, that scene by itself is rarely something to worry about.
Is my cat rubbing its face on me because it loves me?
The short answer is:
It can be part of a positive social relationship, but it means more than one thing.
Cats may rub their head and cheeks against familiar people during comfortable social interaction.
So if your cat voluntarily walks toward you, remains relaxed, presses the forehead against your leg, and rubs the cheeks along you, there is no reason to interpret that as rejection.
Quite the opposite.
The cat is comfortable enough to approach and make physical contact.
Where humans sometimes get carried away is trying to translate the behavior into one exact sentence.
“I love you.”
“You are mine.”
“You are my parent.”
“You have been accepted into the colony.”
We cannot know that any one of these is the precise sentence running through a cat’s mind.
Ansim prefers a less dramatic translation:
“You are familiar, and I am comfortable interacting with you.”
For a cat, that is already a pretty generous review.
Your delivery driver probably does not receive the same greeting.
Why does my cat rub on furniture right after rubbing on me?
Because facial rubbing is not reserved exclusively for the most emotionally important object in the room.
Your cat can have a positive relationship with you and use facial rubbing around familiar environmental objects.
These functions can overlap.
The mistake is assuming:
“My cat rubs me, therefore rubbing must mean love.”
Then:
“My cat rubs the refrigerator, therefore the refrigerator receives equal love.”
That logic gives the refrigerator far too much power.
Instead, think of facial rubbing as one part of the cat’s scent and social world.
You are a familiar social partner.
The sofa is a familiar environmental feature.
Both can belong to the same safe, recognizable home without having identical emotional meaning.





What your cat does
What it may mean
What to watch next




Slides the cheek along a wall or furniture corner and keeps walking
Normal facial rubbing or scent communication
Is the cat otherwise relaxed and behaving normally?


Walks up and rubs the forehead or cheek against your leg
Familiar social interaction may be involved
Did the cat approach voluntarily and remain comfortable?


Rubs faces with another familiar cat
Friendly social contact and scent exchange may be involved
Look at the overall relationship between the cats


Repeatedly rubs only one side of the face
Ear, eye, dental, skin, or facial discomfort may be possible
Check for scratching, head shaking, discharge, pain, or asymmetry


Places the head against a wall and continuously pushes or remains there
Different from normal bunting
Look for changes in awareness, gait, direction, or behavior


Facial rubbing suddenly becomes intense enough to damage skin
Simple scent marking may not explain it
Veterinary assessment is appropriate





What does head bunting look like?
Normal head bunting usually contains movement and purpose.
Imagine a cat walking across the room.
The cat reaches the doorway, places one cheek against the frame, pushes lightly, slides the face past the corner, and continues into the kitchen.
A minute later the same cat walks up to your leg, gives you a forehead bump, rubs along your calf, and heads toward the food bowl.
That is an extremely normal-looking feline schedule.
The cat is moving through the environment.
The contact is brief.
The cat resumes ordinary behavior afterward.
This is very different from a cat that stands strangely in front of a wall and holds or pushes the head against it.
Head bunting vs. head pressing: what is the difference?
This is the most important distinction in this article.
With head bunting, the cheek or forehead contacts the surface as part of a fluid rubbing motion.
The cat usually slides past the object or moves on to something else.
With head pressing, the cat may place the forehead or top of the head against a wall, floor, corner, or solid object and continue pressing or remain abnormally positioned.
The overall cat may also look different.
There may be confusion.
Reduced responsiveness.
Stumbling.
Circling.
Abnormal posture.
Changes in behavior.
The animal may seem as though it does not quite understand where to go next.
This is not a scent-marking question anymore.
It is a medical question.

Is every cat with its head against a wall head pressing?
No.
This distinction is important because pictures online can be frightening.
A cat may sleep with its forehead against the wall.
A cat may briefly lean against a corner while sniffing it.
A cat may rub the forehead against a surface and pause for a second.
None of these automatically means neurologic disease.
Ansim wants you to focus on two things:
duration and context.
Does your cat make normal contact and move on?
Or does the cat repeatedly push the head into the wall and seem abnormal before, during, or afterward?
A still photograph often cannot answer that question.
That is why a short video can be extremely useful.
In one photograph, both cats might simply appear to have a head touching the wall.
Watch thirty seconds of movement and the difference may become much clearer.
Why can head pressing be a medical warning sign?
Head pressing can occur when brain function or neurologic behavior is abnormal.
That does not tell us the exact cause.
Neurologic abnormalities in cats can arise from many different conditions, including inflammatory or infectious disease, metabolic disorders, toxins, structural brain disease, tumors, and other problems.
Owners do not need to diagnose which one is responsible.
What matters at home is recognizing that the behavior is not typical facial rubbing.
If your cat suddenly stands with the head persistently pressed into a surface and also seems confused, walks abnormally, circles, falls, appears poorly responsive, or behaves very differently from normal, veterinary evaluation should not be delayed while you try to determine which diagnosis fits.
At that moment, the question has changed from:
“Why is my cat rubbing the wall?”
to:
“Why is my cat behaving neurologically abnormally?”
What if my cat is circling or stumbling too?
That raises the concern considerably.
A cat that suddenly circles repeatedly, loses balance, stumbles, walks toward inappropriate places, seems mentally altered, or persistently presses the head against a wall should be evaluated promptly.
The combination matters.
A cheek brushing a doorway during an otherwise completely normal walk is one thing.
Head pressing plus altered gait or awareness is another.
If it is safe to do so, record a video.
Do not spend the next hour repeatedly moving your cat away from the wall to see whether the behavior comes back.
Do not test balance at home.
Do not try to prove which side is affected.
Get useful footage if possible, keep the cat safe from stairs or falls, and contact a veterinarian.
The internet will still be there afterward.
Your cat’s neurologic status is the part with a clock attached.
What if my cat rubs only one side of its face?
This deserves a different kind of attention.
Many cats naturally alternate cheeks as they rub against objects.
But if a cat suddenly begins pressing or rubbing one specific side of the face repeatedly and forcefully, especially when that behavior is new, consider whether the cat may be trying to relieve discomfort.
Look for other changes.
Is the cat scratching one ear?
Shaking the head?
Squinting one eye?
Producing unusual eye or ear discharge?
Avoiding hard food?
Dropping food?
Reacting when the jaw or face is touched?
Does one side of the face look different from the other?
Problems involving the ears, eyes, mouth, teeth, skin, or nerves can change how a cat behaves around the face.
The point is not:
“One-sided rubbing means Disease X.”
It is:
“A new one-sided pattern deserves a closer look.”
What if my cat rubs so hard that the skin becomes red?
Normal bunting is generally brief enough that cats go on with their lives.
If repeated rubbing becomes intense enough to cause hair loss, redness, abrasions, or wounds, we need another explanation besides ordinary scent marking.
Itching can cause rubbing.
Pain can cause rubbing.
Ear or facial discomfort can cause rubbing.
An eye problem can make a cat repeatedly work at one side of the face.
Dental or oral discomfort can also change facial behavior.
If your cat is damaging the skin, do not simply assume:
“Wow, somebody is extra affectionate today.”
That would be a fairly unfortunate translation.
The skin damage itself is a good reason for veterinary assessment.
Why does my cat rub its face against another cat?
Cats that live comfortably together may rub their heads or bodies against one another.
This can occur during friendly social interaction and scent exchange.
It can contribute to the familiar chemical environment shared by cats living together.
But, as usual, one behavior does not tell us everything about a relationship.
Two cats can head rub in the morning and still disagree over the best window seat in the afternoon.
We cannot notarize lifelong friendship based on one forehead bump.
Still, if two cats voluntarily approach one another, rub faces, rest comfortably nearby, and show many other relaxed behaviors, those interactions are useful positive clues about their relationship.

If I clean the places my cat rubbed, will my cat be upset?
Cats care about familiar scent.
Humans care about cleaning.
Occasionally, these departments have competing priorities.
Your cat spends the afternoon carefully rubbing the sofa corner.
The next morning you arrive with cleaning supplies.
From the cat’s perspective, the situation may look slightly unreasonable.
“I finished that yesterday.”
You do not need to preserve every rubbed surface forever.
Homes need to be cleaned.
The useful idea is simply to remember that scent familiarity matters to cats.
Suddenly replacing many familiar items, washing every bed at once, deep-cleaning the entire home with strong fragrances, and introducing several new-smelling objects simultaneously may be more disruptive to some cats than ordinary routine cleaning.
You can clean your home without attempting to factory-reset your cat’s entire scent world every weekend.
My cat started rubbing everything after I bought new furniture. Is that normal?
It can be.
Imagine the scene from your cat’s perspective.
Yesterday, the living room smelled familiar.
Today, a gigantic object with unfamiliar factory, warehouse, transport, and human odors has appeared in the middle of it.
Humans call this a new sofa.
The cat may call it:
“Unapproved object pending inspection.”
Facial rubbing can become noticeable as a cat investigates and interacts with new objects.
If your cat walks around the new sofa, rubs the cheek along several corners, explores normally, eats normally, and later relaxes, that behavior alone is not usually concerning.
In Ansim translation:
“Application received. I will add my stamp before final approval.”
Why is my cat rubbing more after moving to a new house?
A new home is an enormous scent change.
New floors.
New walls.
New furniture placement.
Different cleaning products.
Different environmental odors.
Maybe previous occupants or animals.
For a cat, moving can mean rebuilding a familiar scent map from scratch.
Facial rubbing and scratching may become more noticeable while the cat explores and deposits scent information around the new environment.
Keeping some familiar bedding, scratching surfaces, blankets, and other items can help preserve continuity.
But facial rubbing should not distract from the cat’s overall adjustment.
If a recently moved cat is hiding continuously, not eating, avoiding the litter box, vomiting, showing severe fear, or developing major changes in normal daily behavior, the issue is no longer simply:
“My cat is rubbing the new walls.”
Look at the whole cat.
Does increased face rubbing mean my cat is stressed?
Not by itself.
A sudden change in the amount of rubbing can happen during environmental change, but increased facial rubbing is not a standalone diagnosis of anxiety.
This is a good example of why behavior should be interpreted in context.
A new couch arrives and your cat spends ten minutes rubbing around it.
That makes sense.
Your cat begins violently rubbing one cheek against every surface while shaking one ear and scratching until the skin becomes red.
That is a very different story.
Instead of counting the number of rubs, look for what else changed at the same time.
Frequency is information.
It is not a diagnosis.
Should I use a pheromone diffuser to stop face rubbing?
Normal facial rubbing does not need to be “treated.”
It is a natural cat behavior.
Synthetic feline pheromone products may sometimes be used as one part of environmental or behavioral management for particular cats, but there is no reason to use them simply because your healthy cat likes rubbing a cheek against the sofa.
If the real issue is anxiety, intercat conflict, inappropriate elimination, destructive scratching, or another behavior concern, the environment and the individual cat need to be assessed more broadly.
A diffuser is not an off switch for cat behavior.
And ordinary bunting does not need an off switch anyway.
My cat rubs me and then bites. What happened?
This is one of the classic human-cat misunderstandings.
Your cat walks over.
Rub.
Rub.
Rub.
You respond with petting.
A few seconds later:
tap.
nip.
Human reaction:
“Excuse me. Didn’t you just say you loved me?”
The cat did not sign that contract.
Facial rubbing can be a friendly social approach without granting unlimited petting rights.
Some cats enjoy brief, frequent contact and prefer to control when interaction starts and ends.
If your cat rubs against you, try responding with a short, gentle touch around an area the cat normally enjoys, then pause.
If the cat presses closer or reinitiates contact, continue briefly.
If the cat turns away, flicks the tail more sharply, shifts posture, or walks off, let your hand retire as well.
A head rub is not a fifteen-minute full-body massage subscription.
Where should I pet a cat that is head bunting me?
Individual preference matters most.
Some cats that initiate facial contact also enjoy gentle touch around the cheek, chin, forehead, or side of the head.
But there is no universal petting map.
Instead of putting your hand directly into the cat’s face, give the cat an opportunity to approach your hand.
Let the cat place the cheek against you.
Respond briefly.
Pause.
See whether the cat comes back.
If maintaining the interaction requires you to follow the cat around the house with your hand extended, there is a decent chance only one participant is enjoying the event.

My cat never rubs its face on me. Does that mean it doesn’t like me?
No.
This is worth saying clearly.
Cats differ enormously in how they interact socially.
One cat may head-butt your ankle twenty times before breakfast.
Another may rarely rub at all.
That second cat may still choose to sleep beside you, follow you from room to room, slow-blink from the couch, sit nearby, greet you at the door, or simply prefer sharing a room without much physical contact.
Relationships are not graded by bunting frequency.
Some cats express social comfort very physically.
Others are much more understated.
Both can have strong relationships with their people.
Cats, like humans, do not all use the same love language.
Why is video better than a photo when I am worried about head pressing?
Because movement is part of the diagnosis.
A photo freezes the moment.
A cat rubbing past a door frame and a cat standing abnormally with its head against the wall can look surprisingly similar for one fraction of a second.
Video shows what came before.
How the cat approached.
Whether the contact slides across the cheek.
Whether the cat continues walking.
Whether the cat seems coordinated.
Whether the head remains planted.
Whether circling or abnormal posture is present.
If you see something strange, a short video taken safely from a distance can be extremely useful to your veterinarian.
Do not delay urgent care just to obtain the perfect recording.
This is not a wildlife documentary.
Useful is enough.
When should I call a veterinarian about face rubbing?
Routine cheek rubbing against familiar objects in an otherwise normal cat is usually not an emergency.
The picture changes when the behavior itself changes or when other symptoms appear.
Arrange veterinary assessment when facial rubbing becomes unusually forceful or persistent, focuses repeatedly on one side, causes skin damage, or appears together with ear scratching, head shaking, eye changes, mouth discomfort, facial asymmetry, decreased appetite, or other signs of pain.
More urgent assessment is appropriate when a cat appears to be genuinely head pressing and also shows neurologic abnormalities such as circling, severe disorientation, stumbling, collapse, seizures, marked changes in responsiveness, or sudden major behavioral changes.
In those situations, do not spend hours deciding whether the internet calls the movement “rubbing,” “pressing,” “bunting,” or something else.
The abnormal cat is more important than the vocabulary.

How should I respond when my cat rubs against me?
You do not need a complicated protocol.
Your cat approaches.
Rub.
You respond gently if the cat appears comfortable.
Then let the cat decide whether the interaction continues.
Some cats will push the face back into your hand.
Some will rub once and keep walking.
That may be the entire conversation.
From the human perspective, this can feel unsatisfying.
“That’s it?”
Possibly.
Cats are very capable of completing a social transaction in under three seconds.
A quick cheek rub may be less like a declaration of eternal devotion and more like:
“Hello. Confirmed. Carry on.”
You are allowed to appreciate both versions.
So why does my cat rub its face on the wall?
Most of the time, because your cat is being a cat.
Facial rubbing is a normal way of interacting with familiar people, animals, and places through touch and scent.
It does not need to be romanticized into a secret message.
It also does not need to be medicalized simply because the head touched a wall.
What matters is learning the visual difference between a cat that rubs and moves on and a cat that presses and behaves abnormally.
That distinction lets us do two good things at once:
avoid panicking over normal cat behavior,
and avoid dismissing a potentially important neurologic sign as “just another cute cat thing.”
That is exactly where useful observation belongs.

Watching a cat rub its cheek against the corner of a wall can seem like one of the most ordinary moments in the house.
But it tells us something interesting about how cats experience their world.
Humans walk into a room and recognize the furniture.
Cats recognize the furniture too, but they also live inside a landscape of chemical information that we barely perceive.
A favorite corner can carry familiar scent.
Another cat can carry familiar scent.
You can carry familiar scent.
So if your cat brushes its cheek along your leg, walks away, and immediately rubs the sofa, you do not need to compete with the furniture.
You have different jobs.
The sofa holds the cat up.
You open the food.
Your position remains secure.
Just remember the one distinction that matters medically:
A cheek sliding along a wall and a head persistently pressing into a wall are not the same behavior.
When movement, awareness, balance, or personality suddenly changes along with the head behavior, stop translating cat emotions for a moment.
Look at the body first.
Ansim’s Research Notes
Ansim likes ordinary behaviors like facial rubbing because they reveal something we humans easily forget.
We experience a home mostly through what we see.
Cats add another invisible layer.
Scent.
The familiar smell of bedding, furniture, people, and other cats becomes part of the map of home, and facial rubbing is one small way cats interact with that map.
Your leg can be part of it too.
So the next time your cat gently pushes a cheek against your ankle, you do not have to ask:
“Do you love me?”
The fact that your cat voluntarily approached, made comfortable contact, and included you in a familiar social environment already tells you something useful.
And if the cat then walks away and rubs the refrigerator?
Please do not take it personally.
The refrigerator may receive facial scent.
You still control the treat drawer.

[안심이 요약 (new_ansim_summary)]

家の中でも飼い主さんの後ろをずっとついて歩く犬もいれば、「用事があれば呼んでください」という顔で自分の時間を楽しむ犬もいます。この違いには個体の性格や経験だけでなく、犬種がどんな仕事のために作られてきたかも少し関係しています。
牧羊犬やレトリーバーのように人の合図を見ながら協力して働いてきた系統と、嗅覚を頼りに遠くまで追跡したり、自分で判断する必要があったハウンドや一部のテリア、スピッツ系では、人への注目の向け方に平均的な違いが見られることがあります。
ただし犬種は性格の保証書ではありません。ひとりで平気な犬が飼い主さんを愛していないわけでも、ずっと後をついてくる犬のほうが必ずしも健全な愛着を持っているわけでもありません。

F형 공감:
隣の犬は飼い主さんがトイレに入っただけでドアの前で待っているのに、うちの犬は私が帰宅しても片目だけ開けてまた寝る。そんなとき、飼い主さんの心には静かな疑問が浮かびます。「私、毎月ちゃんとフード代を払ってるよね……私たち、仲良しだよね？」
[검증된 근거 (Evidence)]

핵심 인사이트 (keyInsight):

犬は歴史的に、牧畜、回収、嗅覚追跡、狩猟、警護、そり引きなど、異なる仕事のために選択繁殖されてきました。大規模な遺伝・行動研究では、こうした作業歴と犬種系統ごとの平均的な行動傾向に関連があることが示されています。牧羊犬やレトリーバー系統では比較的高い訓練性や人の指示への反応が見られやすく、嗅覚ハウンド系統では、人の指示を待ち続けるよりも匂いを追って独立して働く歴史と一致する傾向が確認されています。
一方で犬種は個体の性格を完全には決めません。18,000頭を超える純血種・ミックス犬の行動データを分析した研究では、行動特性に遺伝的要素がある一方で、現代の犬種が個体レベルの行動差を説明する割合は限定的でした。同じ犬種の中でも性格差は大きく、社会化、訓練、生活環境、年齢、過去の経験、個体差が実際の行動に大きく影響します。

주의 사항 (cautionNote):

独立心と飼い主との関係の弱さを混同しないでください。普段は人とよく関わる犬が急に触られることを嫌がり、遊ばなくなり、食欲や睡眠まで変化した場合は、単なる「マイペースな性格」ではなく痛みや不安、病気の可能性も確認する必要があります。また、常に飼い主について回る行動も、それだけで愛情が深いとは限りません。ひとりになると強い不安や破壊行動、鳴き続ける、脱出を試みるなどの行動がある場合は、分離関連問題として別に評価する必要があります。

家に2頭の犬がいると想像してみてください。
1頭目は、飼い主さんがソファから立てば一緒に立ちます。キッチンへ行けばついてきて、洗面所へ行ってもついてきます。トイレに入れば、今度はドアの前で待機です。
飼い主さんがくしゃみをすると、すぐに顔を上げます。
「大丈夫ですか？ 何かお手伝いしましょうか？」
ほぼ24時間対応の専属秘書です。
一方、2頭目はまったく違います。
飼い主さんが帰宅しました。
「ただいま！」
犬が顔を上げます。
一度見ます。
「確認しました。」
という顔をして、また寝ます。
ところが10分後、おやつの袋が開いた瞬間。
ものすごい速さで現れます。
飼い主さんは思います。
「私があなたを養っているんだよね？ なんで私が雇われている感じがするの？」
そこで今日は、アンシムがかなり非公式な分類を作ってみました。
サービス精神旺盛な犬と、必要なときだけ営業する犬。
もちろん獣医行動学の教科書にこんな分類はありません。

つまり、飼い主さんを無視しているのではなく、
問題解決を担当する部署が違う
だけかもしれません。
どちらの性格が「いい犬」なの？
答えは意外と単純です。
飼い主さんの生活に合う性格が、いい性格です。
毎日一緒にトレーニングやドッグスポーツを楽しみたい人なら、人と協力する欲求の強い犬はとても楽しいでしょう。
一方、在宅勤務中に30秒ごとに前足でキーボードを押しながら、
「今すぐ私に注目してください。」
と要求されたら、手厚いサービスが少し過剰サービスに感じるかもしれません。
独立的な犬は最初は少し淡白に見えるかもしれません。
でも自分で落ち着いて休めることや、ひとりの時間を過ごせる能力は、家庭によっては非常に大きな長所です。
性格に絶対的な上下はありません。
「人が大好き」には長所と管理ポイントがあります。
「独立心が強い」にも長所と管理ポイントがあります。
犬の性格は年齢とともに変わる？
ある程度は変わります。
比較的安定する性格傾向もありますが、行動は経験や環境の影響を受け続けます。
若い犬では活動量や注意要求が強く、成犬になるにつれてひとりで休む時間が増えることがあります。
新しい家庭に迎えられた犬も、環境に慣れるにつれて行動が変わることがあります。
訓練によって、人の合図への反応も変化します。
つまり遺伝はスタート地点の一つで、
生活がその上にずっと書き足されていきます。
だから、
「この犬種はこうだから。」
という一言で全部を終わらせてしまうのは、少しもったいないんです。
うちの犬はどちらのタイプ？ 家で楽しく観察してみよう
テストというより、遊び感覚で見てください。
飼い主さんが別の部屋へ移動したとき、犬はすぐについてきますか？
それとも、そのまま安心して寝ていますか？
新しい問題に出会ったとき、自分で先に試しますか？
それとも早い段階で飼い主さんの顔を見ますか？
散歩中、人の合図と匂いではどちらに気持ちが向きやすいでしょう。
一緒に遊んでいる途中で飼い主さんが手を止めたとき、
「続けてください。」
とすぐ要求しますか？
それとも、
「わかりました。では自分の予定に戻ります。」
と去りますか？
これを点数化して、
「うちの犬、甘えん坊指数82点。」
と判定する必要はありません。
その犬が世界をどう見ているのかを知ることが目的です。
犬をよく知るということは、犬種説明を暗記するより、こういう小さなパターンを知ることに近いのかもしれません。

急に「マイペース」になったなら、性格だけで片づけないで
最後に、ここは少し大事な話です。
もともとひとりで過ごすのが好きな犬と、
以前は人とよく関わっていたのに急に避けるようになった犬
は同じではありません。
普段は触られるのが好きだった犬が急に嫌がる。
遊ばなくなる。
抱っこを避ける。
食欲や睡眠まで変わる。
そんな変化があるなら、
「年をとってマイペースになったのかな。」
だけで終わらせないほうがいいでしょう。
痛みや体調不良、不安でも、人との関わり方は変わります。
逆に、急に強くべったりするようになることもあります。
性格にはある程度の連続性があります。
だから大切なのは、
「この犬種はどういう性格？」
よりも、
「これは、うちの子にとっていつもの姿？」
と考えることです。
アンシムの研究ノート
今日の記事は、かなり科学者らしくない分類から始まりました。
サービス精神旺盛な犬。
必要なときだけ営業する犬。
でも最後まで読んでいただいた今なら、少し違って見えるかもしれません。
ある犬は、飼い主さんを頻繁に確認し、一緒に何かすることが大好きです。
ある犬は、自分で探索し、自分で判断し、ひとりで過ごすことも得意です。
その差には、犬種が作られてきた歴史も少し含まれています。
牧羊犬やレトリーバーのように、人と近くで協力してきた犬。
ハウンド、一部のテリア、そり犬のように、自分で判断する必要があった犬。
人の合図の使い方に平均的な違いが見られるのは、不思議ではありません。
でも犬種名は性格表の全部ではありません。
大規模研究でも、同じ犬種内の行動差は非常に大きいことがわかっています。
だからゴールデンレトリーバーが全員、無制限の愛情サービスを提供するわけではありません。
柴犬のカスタマーサービス営業時間が1日15分と決まっているわけでもありません。
そして、独立的な犬が飼い主さんをあまり好きではないわけでもありません。
ずっと身体を寄せている犬もいます。
少し離れた場所で寝ながら、飼い主さんが立ったら一度だけ静かに確認する犬もいます。
どちらも関係です。
どちらも信頼かもしれません。
アンシムは、むしろこの違いこそ犬と暮らす面白さだと思っています。
人間の家族だって、全員が一日中くっついて生活しているわけではありませんから。
だから仕事から帰ってきたとき、愛犬が尻尾を3回だけ振ってまた寝ても、あまり落ち込まないでください。
10分後に冷蔵庫を開けてみましょう。
その瞬間、
今まで隠していた驚くほど高い社交性が突然発見されるかもしれません。

ContentText:
[안심이 요약 (new_ansim_summary)]

Some dogs follow their people from room to room, watch every hand signal, and seem permanently available for emotional support, while others are perfectly happy saying hello once and returning to their own business.
Part of that difference can reflect what breeds were historically selected to do: retrievers and herding dogs often worked closely with human direction, while many scent hounds, terriers, spitz-type dogs, and other independent workers had to make more decisions on their own.
Breed gives us clues, not a personality guarantee; a dog who enjoys independence is not necessarily less attached, and a dog who follows you everywhere is not automatically more securely bonded.

F형 공감:
If your neighbor’s dog waits outside the bathroom like a tiny security guard while yours barely opens one eye when you come home, it is completely understandable to wonder, “Excuse me, I pay for the food around here—are we actually friends?”
[검증된 근거 (Evidence)]

핵심 인사이트 (keyInsight):

Dog breeds were historically selected for very different jobs, including herding, retrieving, scent tracking, guarding, hunting, and pulling. Large-scale genetic and behavioral research has found that these working histories are associated with average behavioral tendencies across breed lineages. Herding and retriever lineages, for example, tend to show relatively high trainability and responsiveness to human direction, while scent-hound lineages reflect a history of working more independently while following odor trails.
At the same time, breed does not determine an individual dog’s personality. A large study involving more than 18,000 purebred and mixed-breed dogs found that modern breed explained only a modest portion of behavioral variation at the individual level. Dogs within the same breed can differ dramatically because genetics interacts with early experience, socialization, training, household environment, age, and individual temperament.

주의 사항 (cautionNote):

Do not confuse independence with a weak bond, or clinginess with a healthier bond. If a normally social dog suddenly avoids touch, interaction, play, or family members, pain, fear, or illness may need to be considered. Likewise, a dog who constantly follows a person but becomes highly distressed when left alone may have a separation-related problem rather than simply being “extra loving.”

[본문 내용 (Content)]
Imagine two dogs living in the same house.
Dog number one follows the owner to the kitchen.
Then the bedroom.
Then the front door.
Then the bathroom.
The owner sneezes.
The dog immediately looks up.
“Are you all right? Do you require assistance?”
This dog is basically a 24-hour personal assistant with fur.
Now meet dog number two.
The owner comes home.
“Hi! I’m home!”
The dog lifts its head.
Makes eye contact.
Acknowledges receipt of the information.
Then goes back to sleep.
Ten minutes later, someone opens a bag of treats.
Suddenly the dog has discovered an astonishing capacity for social engagement.
And somewhere in the living room, a human quietly thinks:
“I’m pretty sure I’m raising you. Why does it feel like you hired me?”
That brings us to today’s completely unofficial Ansim classification system:
The full-service dog versus the independent contractor.
No, you will not find those categories in a veterinary behavior textbook.
If Ansim submitted “full-service dog” as a scientific phenotype, someone would probably revoke his magnifying glass.
But as a way to describe what owners actually experience at home?
It works surprisingly well.
Some dogs seem to offer affection, attention, eye contact, cooperation, and emotional support on an unlimited plan.
Others operate more like:
“Services available as needed. Terms and conditions apply.”
Here is the important part.
The second dog does not necessarily love you less.
How dogs interact with people is shaped by breed history, inherited tendencies, learning, socialization, household experience, and individual personality.
And once you look at that history, some of these differences start making a lot more sense.

First, a disclaimer: “Velcro dog” and “independent dog” are not scientific personality diagnoses
Let’s install the safety rail before the jokes get out of control.
Dogs do not scientifically fall into two categories called “devoted” and “self-employed.”
Real canine behavior is much more complicated.
Behavior questionnaires such as C-BARQ evaluate multiple traits separately, including trainability, excitability, fear, chasing behavior, attachment and attention-seeking, and other dimensions.
That means one dog can be extremely affectionate and stubborn.
Another can enjoy sleeping alone but be wonderfully responsive in training.
A dog can love people and still say:
“I would prefer not to sit directly on your rib cage tonight.”
Humans are like this too.
Being introverted does not make someone unfriendly.
Being outgoing does not automatically make someone emotionally secure.
Dogs deserve the same nuance.
For the sake of today’s article, though, we will use two playful labels.
A dog who frequently checks in with people, follows them, and readily works with human signals will be our full-service or Velcro-type dog.
A dog who places more value on independent exploration and self-directed activity will be our independent contractor.
Neither is better.
But they are very different roommates.

What does a “full-service” dog feel like to live with?
For this kind of dog, the human is a major source of information.
You stand up.
The dog stands up.
You walk toward the kitchen.
The dog would like to know why.
Something unfamiliar happens outside.
The dog looks at your face first.
During training, these dogs may seem to be asking:
“What are we doing next?”
Throw the ball.
They bring it back.
Throw it again.
They bring it back again.
Again.
Again.
Eventually the human is the one requesting a union-mandated break.
Some of this human-oriented behavior makes sense when we look at the jobs certain dogs were historically selected to perform.
Many herding dogs needed to coordinate closely with a person while controlling livestock.
Retrievers needed to work with hunters, respond to direction, locate game, and bring it back.
Across large behavioral datasets, several herding and retriever lineages show tendencies consistent with high trainability and close cooperation with people.
Translated into Ansim language:
“Boss, I’m available. What’s the assignment?”
What about the dog who appears to have its own calendar?
Now picture a Beagle on a walk.
The owner says:
“Come!”
The Beagle smells the grass.
“Buddy!”
Still smelling.
“Treat!”
One ear moves approximately three millimeters.
Progress.
Then a more interesting scent arrives from a bush.
Meeting adjourned.
This does not necessarily mean the dog dislikes the owner.
Many scent hounds were selected to follow odor trails with substantial independence. Their job was not always to stare continuously at a human waiting for the next instruction.
A dog whose ancestors benefited from staying focused on scent may naturally distribute attention differently from a dog whose ancestors benefited from constantly checking a shepherd’s position.
Large-scale genetic and behavioral research has found relatively lower average human-directed trainability in some scent-hound lineages, which fits that historical working style.
The dog may not be ignoring you.
You may simply be ranked below “mysterious smell from 45 minutes ago” at that particular moment.
From the human perspective, admittedly, the result feels similar.
“I lost to a bush.”





Ansim-style type
What owners often notice

Which breeds tend to feel more “full-service”?
Now we get to the fun part.
But please keep this sentence nearby:
Breed tendencies are averages, not personality warranties.
A Golden Retriever can be independent.
A Shiba can be your shadow.
A Beagle can have excellent recall.
And somewhere, statistically speaking, there is probably a Border Collie who has decided that naps are a legitimate career path.
Golden Retriever: “Need anything? That? This? I can carry it.”
Golden Retrievers are almost cultural shorthand for human-friendly cooperation.
Their retriever heritage involved working with people to locate and recover game.
That kind of job rewards attention to human direction and willingness to keep participating in a shared task.
Retriever lineages also tend to score relatively high in trainability measures in large behavioral datasets.
In Ansim’s completely unofficial customer-service index, that can feel very generous.
Look at human.
Listen to human.
Retrieve object.
Return object.
Receive praise.
Repeat until one party collapses.
The possible downside is that Golden Retriever customer service may occasionally extend to everyone.
A visitor enters the house.
The dog says:
“Welcome. First time here? Wonderful. Would you like to see my belly?”
Labrador Retriever: cooperation, snacks, and questionable furniture decisions
Labradors come from a similar broad working tradition.
Close cooperation with people mattered.
Responding to human direction mattered.
Retrieving things mattered.
That does not mean every Labrador arrives preinstalled with perfect manners.
Anyone who has lived with an adolescent Labrador knows an important scientific truth:
A dog can be highly cooperative and still attempt to eat a sofa cushion.
Friendly personality and furniture survival are separate variables.
Border Collie: “No assignment? I can create one.”
Border Collies were selected for extremely close coordination with humans while managing livestock.
Attention to movement, directional cues, and human communication could be highly valuable.
Research comparing cooperative and more independent working breeds has also found differences in how readily dogs use or seek human information in certain tasks.
Calling the Border Collie merely a Velcro dog almost feels insufficient.
This is closer to the high-performing employee who has already opened three projects before management arrives.
The challenge?
If there is no work, some dogs may invent work.
Children running?
Potential livestock.
Cat moving?
Potential livestock.
Vacuum cleaner?
Apparently livestock.
The human concept of
“Nothing needs to happen right now.”
may require careful explanation.

Which breeds can feel more like independent contractors?
Now let’s visit the other side of the office.
And one more reminder:
Independent does not mean bad.
For many historical jobs, independent decision-making was an advantage.
Beagle: “I heard you. Unfortunately, the smell is urgent.”
Scent hounds experience the world through information humans cannot access.
You are calling your Beagle.
Meanwhile the Beagle’s nose may be receiving:
“Chihuahua passed here 32 minutes ago.”
“Chicken crumb discovered yesterday.”
“Cat crossed this route at 4:13 a.m.”
You cannot compete with that amount of breaking news using one cheerful “Come!”
Research on breed lineages supports the idea that scent hounds, on average, can show lower human-oriented trainability than several highly cooperative lineages.
That is not the same as low intelligence.
A dog designed to independently follow a scent does not need to solve every problem by staring at a human face.
The Beagle may be thinking:
“You are important. But the smell is live.”
Dachshund: Ansim declines to comment
This section creates a professional conflict of interest.
Dachshunds were historically developed to pursue quarry into burrows, where independent decision-making mattered.
Inside a tunnel, the human cannot stand beside the dog saying:
“Left. No, your other left. Sit. Wait. Good boy.”
The dog has to make choices.
That historical independence does not determine the personality of every modern Dachshund, but self-directed behavior is not exactly shocking in the breed.
Ansim has been advised by his legal department not to make further comments.
He will only acknowledge the existence of Dachshunds who ignore humans for twenty minutes and then display breathtaking obedience the instant a refrigerator opens.
Shiba Inu: “I love you. I simply do not require continuous physical contact.”
Some ancient and spitz-type lineages have shown lower average attachment or attention-seeking scores than several other breed clusters in owner-reported behavioral research.
Those measures can include following people through the home, seeking physical proximity, and requesting attention.
This is where people make a very unfair leap:
“Shibas don’t love their owners.”
No.
Independent working breeds can form strong attachment relationships with people too.
A dog can feel secure with you without turning itself into a furry bracelet.
The Shiba on the opposite side of the couch may be perfectly content.
Its love language simply may not be:
“I must remain attached to your thigh at all times.”
Human translation:
“I like you very much. Why would that require us to share the same cushion?”
Siberian Husky: independent, but not necessarily quiet about it
Siberian Huskies also come from a working history in which dogs sometimes needed stamina, group coordination, and situational independence rather than constant moment-by-moment human instruction.
So yes, they can feel wonderfully self-directed.
But “emotionally distant” would be a risky description.
Many Husky owners know the issue is not a lack of communication.
It is often the opposite.
Human:
“Walk is over.”
Husky:
“Awooooo.”
“We’re going home.”
“Awoooooo.”
“Yes, home.”
“AAAAWOOOOOO.”
Communication is excellent.
Consensus is poor.
Why can two dogs of the same breed be completely different?
This is the most important section in the entire article.
Breed differences are real at the population level.
But variation within a breed is enormous.
A large Science study analyzing behavioral information from more than 18,000 dogs found that many behaviors show heritable components, yet modern breed explained only a modest share of individual behavioral variation.
In other words:
Breed is a clue.
It is not destiny.
A Golden Retriever can love solitude.
A Shiba can follow someone into every room.
A Beagle can become beautifully responsive to recall training.
A Border Collie can prefer sleeping to reorganizing the household.
Genes are only part of the story.
Socialization, learning history, household structure, reinforcement, previous experiences, age, and the dog’s own temperament all influence behavior.
Dogs do not arrive as photocopies of the breed description.
Thankfully.
Otherwise living with them would be far less interesting.
“My dog ignores me when I call. Is he just stubborn?”
Humans are very quick to turn behavior into personality judgments.
“He’s stubborn.”
“She doesn’t respect me.”
“He knows what I want. He just doesn’t care.”
Behavior usually becomes clearer when we ask more practical questions.
What is competing for the dog’s attention?
How strong is the learned cue?
What usually happens after the dog responds?
For example, a scent hound exploring a fascinating smell may value that odor more than the owner’s voice at that moment.
A dog may also simply have weak recall training.
Or imagine this pattern:
Every time the owner says “Come,” the dog returns and the walk immediately ends.
Eventually the dog learns:
Come = fun is over.
Then the dog hesitates to come.
Technically, that is not failed learning.
That is excellent learning with unfortunate curriculum design.
If my dog follows me everywhere, does that mean we have an amazing bond?
Not automatically.
Enjoying proximity is perfectly normal.
Many dogs genuinely love staying near their people.
But there is a difference between:
“I enjoy being with you.”
and:
“I cannot function if you disappear behind the bathroom door for 40 seconds.”
If a dog cries intensely, scratches doors, destroys objects, attempts to escape, or shows severe distress when separated, that may be a separation-related problem rather than simply impressive devotion.
Behavior assessment tools also distinguish attachment or attention-seeking from separation-related behavior.
So this sentence:
“My dog literally cannot live without me.”
may sound romantic.
Behaviorally, we would prefer:
“My dog enjoys being with me and can also feel safe when I am temporarily unavailable.”
A truly full-service dog does not have to operate a 24-hour emergency call center.
Does a dog who plays alone have a weaker relationship with the owner?
Not at all.
For many households, this is an excellent skill.
You read a book.
The dog naps in another room.
You work.
The dog chews its toy.
You leave briefly.
Civilization remains intact.
Then, when it is time for a walk, the dog meets you at the door.
When something feels frightening, it looks for you.
When you initiate play, it happily participates.
That can be a very healthy relationship.
Research comparing dogs from more cooperative and more independent working backgrounds suggests that both can form attachment relationships with human caregivers.
The style of interaction may differ.
Attachment itself is not limited to dogs that physically follow a person all day.
Human friendships are similar.
Someone who texts you fifty times a day is not automatically a better friend than someone who checks in once a week.
Proximity and relationship quality are not the same measurement.
Does trainability mean a dog loves people more?
No.
Trainability and attachment are separate behavioral dimensions.
A trainable dog may respond reliably to cues, pay close attention to human actions, learn routines quickly, and remain focused despite distractions.
Attachment and attention-seeking refer to behaviors such as following a person, requesting interaction, and seeking physical proximity.
A dog can be brilliant in training and then happily sleep alone.
Another dog can spend the entire evening pressed against its person—and completely forget its own name the moment the front door opens.
To owners of the second group, Ansim offers quiet support.
Love and obedience are not the same subject in school.

Ansim’s completely unofficial breed personality chart
This is not a scientific ranking.
Think of it as a playful translation of historical working styles into everyday roommate behavior.

What owners may notice

Please notice what this table does not say.
It does not say every Golden Retriever is affectionate.
It does not say every Beagle has poor recall.
It does not say every Shiba is aloof.
And it absolutely does not justify meeting a Shiba for the first time and saying:
“Oh, they’re kind of rude, right?”
Imagine being assigned a personality before you have even sniffed the person.
Dogs deserve better.
Do some dogs really “give everything” to their owners?
We should be careful not to translate dog behavior too literally into human emotion.
A dog follows you.
Brings a toy.
Makes eye contact.
Sits beside you.
We cannot confirm that the dog is internally thinking:
“I hereby transfer all emotional assets to my beloved human.”
But dogs are extraordinarily social with people.
They use human gestures and attention.
They form attachment relationships with caregivers.
And some breed lineages were historically selected to work in close coordination with humans.
For those dogs, interacting and cooperating with a person can itself be highly rewarding.
That can look extremely generous from our side.
Almost suspiciously generous.
Is an independent dog selfish?
“Selfish” is a human moral judgment.
It is not a particularly useful behavioral diagnosis.
A dog bred to solve problems at a distance from people may naturally approach the world differently from a dog bred to continuously monitor a handler.
A Border Collie working livestock and a hound following scent did not need the same style of human attention.
That does not make one more loving.
Their problem-solving departments are simply different.
Border Collie:
“What does management think?”
Beagle:
“I’ll submit a report after field investigation.”
Shiba:
“May I ask why management approval is required?”
Dachshund:
“Decision already made.”
Which personality is better?
The answer is wonderfully boring:
The personality that fits your life.
If you love training, dog sports, frequent interaction, and shared activities, a dog with strong human-cooperation tendencies may be incredibly rewarding.
If you work from home and your dog taps your keyboard every thirty seconds because:
“Please direct all attention to the dog department.”
the same trait may become exhausting.
An independent dog can initially feel less dramatic.
But a dog that can relax alone, entertain itself safely, and enjoy personal space may fit certain households beautifully.
There is no universal hierarchy.
Highly social dogs have strengths and management needs.
Independent dogs have strengths and management needs.
Compatibility matters more than winning a personality contest.
Can a dog’s personality change with age?
Yes, to a degree.
Some temperament traits remain relatively stable, but behavior continues to be shaped by learning and life experience.
Dogs may change after adoption as they become comfortable in a new household.
Young dogs may show more activity, attention-seeking, and difficulty settling.
Adults may become more comfortable resting independently.
Training changes how dogs respond to people.
Routine changes behavior.
Health changes behavior.
Experience keeps writing on top of genetics.
That is why the sentence:
“This breed is just like that.”
can sometimes close the conversation too early.
Breed history may help explain the starting point.
Life continues editing the document.
How can you tell which style your dog prefers?
Do not turn this into a formal personality exam.
Just watch.
When you move to another room, does your dog follow automatically, or remain comfortably where it is?
When the dog encounters a new problem, does it try several solutions independently or look toward you early?
On walks, how easily does human communication compete with smells and movement?
During play, when you stop, does your dog immediately ask you to restart?
Or does it say:
“Very well. I have other projects.”
These observations are more useful than assigning a score such as:
“My dog is 84% Velcro.”
The goal is not to rank the dog.
It is to understand how that dog experiences the world.
Knowing your dog is less about memorizing the breed description and more about recognizing these tiny everyday patterns.

When “independent” suddenly becomes “withdrawn,” pay attention
There is one important distinction owners should know.
A dog that has always enjoyed personal space is not the same as a dog that suddenly starts avoiding people.
If your normally social dog begins moving away from touch, stops playing, avoids being picked up, sleeps differently, loses appetite, or becomes unusually irritable, do not simply decide that the dog has “become independent.”
Pain and illness can change social behavior.
Likewise, sudden clinginess can sometimes appear when a dog is uncomfortable, frightened, aging, or experiencing changes in the environment.
Personality tends to have continuity.
A sudden behavioral shift deserves curiosity.
Sometimes the most useful question is not:
“What kind of dog is this?”
but:
“Is this still normal for my dog?”
Ansim’s Research Note
Today’s article began with a very unserious classification system.
The full-service dog.
The independent contractor.
But by now, hopefully, those labels sound a little different.
Some dogs naturally check in with people constantly and seem happiest doing things together.
Others are more comfortable exploring, resting, and solving problems on their own.
Part of that difference can reflect the jobs their ancestors were selected to do.
Herding and retriever lineages often benefited from close human cooperation.
Scent hounds and other independent workers sometimes benefited from persistence and autonomous decision-making.
But breed never tells the whole story.
Large-scale research shows enormous behavioral variation within breeds, and modern breed labels explain only a limited portion of an individual dog’s behavior.
So a Golden Retriever is not contractually obligated to provide unlimited affection.
And a Shiba Inu does not operate customer service for only fifteen minutes per day.
An independent dog does not necessarily love you less.
Some dogs show their relationship by leaning against you whenever you sit down.
Others sleep across the room, quietly check where you are when you stand up, and then continue their nap.
Both can be attachment.
Both can be trust.
And Ansim thinks that difference is part of what makes living with dogs so interesting.
Humans do not all love in exactly the same way either.
So if you come home from work, your dog gives you three tail wags and immediately goes back to sleep, try not to take it personally.
Wait ten minutes.
Then open the refrigerator.
You may discover that your dog has been hiding an extraordinary capacity for social connection all along.

Title: 혜자스러운 강아지 vs 창렬스러운 강아지? 주인에게 다 주는 개와 마이웨이견의 차이
Excerpt: [안심이 요약 (new_ansim_summary)] 어떤 강아지는 집 안에서도 보호자를 졸졸 따라다니며 눈을 맞추고 무엇이든 함께하려 하고, 어떤 강아지는 “볼일 있으면 부르세요”라는 듯 자기 생활을 더 중요하게 여깁니다. 이런 차이에는 개체 성격과 경험뿐 아니라 품종이 만들어진 작업 목적도 어느 정도 영향을 줄 수 있습니다. 목양견·리트리버처럼 사람의 신호를 보며 협력하도록 선택된 계통과, 후각을 따라 멀리 이동하거나 독립적으로 판단해야 […]
ContentText:
[안심이 요약 (new_ansim_summary)]

어떤 강아지는 집 안에서도 보호자를 졸졸 따라다니며 눈을 맞추고 무엇이든 함께하려 하고, 어떤 강아지는 “볼일 있으면 부르세요”라는 듯 자기 생활을 더 중요하게 여깁니다. 이런 차이에는 개체 성격과 경험뿐 아니라 품종이 만들어진 작업 목적도 어느 정도 영향을 줄 수 있습니다.
목양견·리트리버처럼 사람의 신호를 보며 협력하도록 선택된 계통과, 후각을 따라 멀리 이동하거나 독립적으로 판단해야 했던 하운드·일부 테리어·스피츠 계통은 사람에게 주의를 기울이는 방식에서 평균적인 차이를 보일 수 있습니다. 하지만 이것은 어디까지나 경향이지, 개별 강아지의 성격을 품종 이름만으로 결정할 수 있다는 뜻은 아닙니다.
보호자를 덜 따라다니고 혼자 잘 논다고 애착이 약한 강아지도 아닙니다. 독립 작업형과 협력 작업형 품종 모두 보호자와 애착을 형성할 수 있으며, 훈련과 생활환경·사회화 경험도 실제 행동에 큰 영향을 줍니다.

F형 공감:“옆집 강아지는 보호자가 화장실만 가도 문 앞에서 기다리는데 우리 집 강아지는 제가 퇴근해도 눈만 한번 뜨고 다시 잔다면, 집사님 마음에 작은 의문이 피어납니다. ‘내가 밥값을 이렇게 하는데… 우리 관계 맞지?’ 안심이가 오늘은 그 서운함을 과학과 약간의 유머로 풀어볼게요.”

[검증된 근거 (Evidence)]

핵심 인사이트 (keyInsight):

개 품종은 역사적으로 목축, 회수, 사냥, 경비, 썰매 끌기 등 서로 다른 일을 수행하도록 선택되어 왔고, 이런 선택은 행동적 경향과도 관련됩니다. 4,000마리 이상의 개과동물 유전자료와 약 47,000마리의 C-BARQ 행동자료를 분석한 연구에서는 목양견·리트리버 등 일부 계통에서 높은 훈련가능성 같은 경향이, 후각하운드 계통에서는 독립적으로 냄새를 추적하는 작업 역사와 일치하는 상대적으로 낮은 인간 지향적 훈련가능성 경향이 확인됐습니다.
하지만 품종은 개체 행동을 완전히 결정하지 않습니다. 18,385마리의 순종·믹스견 행동자료를 분석한 연구에서는 행동 특성에 유전적 요소가 존재하면서도 현대 품종이 개체 수준 행동 변이의 약 9%만 설명했습니다. 또한 같은 품종 안에서도 행동 차이가 매우 큽니다. 따라서 “골든은 무조건 다정하다”, “시바는 무조건 주인을 무시한다” 같은 판단은 과학적으로 지나친 일반화입니다.

주의 사항 (cautionNote):

독립적인 성향과 보호자와의 관계 문제를 혼동하지 마세요. 평소 혼자 잘 지내던 강아지가 갑자기 사람을 피하거나 접촉을 싫어하고, 놀이·식욕·수면까지 달라졌다면 단순한 ‘마이웨이 성격’이 아니라 통증이나 불안, 질병 같은 변화를 확인할 필요가 있습니다. 또한 사람에게 지나치게 붙어 다니는 행동도 무조건 애정이 깊다는 뜻은 아니며, 보호자가 사라졌을 때 심하게 불안해하거나 파괴행동·울음·탈출 시도를 보인다면 분리 관련 문제를 따로 평가해야 합니다.

[본문 내용 (Content)]
집에 두 마리의 강아지가 있다고 상상해볼게요.
첫 번째 강아지는 보호자가 소파에 앉으면 옆에 붙습니다. 주방에 가면 따라갑니다. 화장실에 가면 문 앞에서 대기합니다. 택배를 받으러 현관에 나가도 따라옵니다.
보호자가 재채기라도 하면 고개를 번쩍 듭니다.
“괜찮으십니까? 제가 도와드릴 일이라도?”
거의 24시간 전담 비서입니다.
반면 두 번째 강아지는 같은 집에서 전혀 다른 인생을 삽니다.
보호자가 퇴근했습니다.
“나 왔어!”
강아지가 고개를 듭니다.
한 번 봅니다. 다시 잡니다.
간식 봉지가 열리는 순간에만 놀라운 속도로 나타납니다.
보호자는 점점 서운해집니다.
“얘야, 내가 너를 키우는 거야. 네가 나를 고용한 게 아니야.”
그래서 오늘 안심이가 아주 비공식적인 분류법을 하나 만들어봤습니다.
혜자스러운 강아지와 창렬스러운 강아지.
물론 수의행동학 교과서에는 이런 분류가 없습니다.
논문 검색창에 혜자견을 입력하면 안심이의 연구원 자격부터 의심받을 가능성이 큽니다.
하지만 보호자가 체감하는 강아지 성격 차이를 설명하기에는 묘하게 정확한 표현입니다.
어떤 아이는 자기가 가진 관심과 애정을 거의 무제한 정액제처럼 제공합니다.
반면 어떤 아이는 필요한 순간에만 정확히 서비스를 제공합니다.
하지만 재미있는 건 여기서부터입니다.
후자의 강아지가 보호자를 덜 사랑한다고 단정할 수는 없습니다.
강아지가 사람을 대하는 방식에는 품종의 역사와 유전적 경향, 어린 시절 경험, 훈련과 생활환경, 그리고 무엇보다 개체 성격이 함께 들어가기 때문입니다.

먼저 알아두세요: 혜자견과 창렬견은 과학적 성격분류가 아닙니다
오늘 글의 안전장치부터 하나 설치하겠습니다.
혜자형과 창렬형은 이해를 돕기 위한 안심이식 별명입니다.
과학적으로 개의 성격은 그렇게 두 종류로 나뉘지 않습니다.
실제로 C-BARQ 같은 행동평가 도구에서는 훈련가능성, 흥분성, 사람이나 개에 대한 공포, 추적 행동, 애착·관심추구 등 여러 행동 특성을 각각 평가합니다.
즉 한 강아지가 사람을 잘 따라다니면서도 고집이 셀 수 있고, 혼자 잘 지내면서도 훈련은 아주 잘될 수 있습니다.
사람으로 치면
“내향적이니까 불친절하다.”
라고 말할 수 없는 것과 비슷합니다.
강아지도 하나의 축으로 성격을 다 설명할 수 없습니다.
그래도 오늘은 재미있게 읽기 위해,
보호자에게 관심을 많이 표현하고 인간의 지시에 적극적으로 반응하는 쪽을 ‘혜자형’, 자기 판단과 자기 활동의 비중이 큰 쪽을 ‘마이웨이형’ 또는 우리의 문제적 별명 ‘창렬형’이라고 불러보겠습니다.

혜자스러운 강아지는 어떤 느낌일까요?
혜자형 강아지는 보호자의 존재 자체가 꽤 중요한 정보입니다.
집에서 보호자가 움직이면 같이 움직이고, 뭔가 새로운 일이 생기면 사람의 얼굴부터 확인하는 경우가 많습니다.
훈련할 때도 사람의 손짓과 말에 집중하고,
“다음은 뭐 하면 돼?” 하는 느낌을 줍니다.
공을 던지면 물어오고, 다시 던져달라고 가져옵니다.
또 가져옵니다. 또 가져옵니다. 보호자가 먼저 체력 고갈을 선언합니다.
이런 사람 지향적인 행동경향은 역사적으로 인간과 가까이 협력하며 일을 해야 했던 일부 품종군에서 평균적으로 더 두드러질 수 있습니다.
목양견은 사람이 보내는 방향과 명령을 보면서 가축을 움직여야 했고, 리트리버는 사냥한 새의 위치와 사람의 신호를 이용해 회수해야 했습니다. 실제 연구에서도 목양견과 리트리버를 포함한 작업 계통에서 상대적으로 높은 훈련가능성과 인간의 신호를 활용하는 경향이 확인됩니다.
안심이식으로 번역하면,
“사장님, 업무지시 기다리고 있겠습니다.” 형입니다.
반대로 창렬스러운… 아니, 독립적인 강아지는 어떤 느낌일까요?
이번에는 산책 중인 비글을 떠올려볼게요.
보호자가 말합니다.
“이리 와.” 비글은 냄새를 맡습니다.
“비글아!” 계속 냄새를 맡습니다.
“간식!” 귀가 아주 미세하게 움직입니다.
그런데 저쪽 풀숲에서 더 흥미로운 냄새가 발견됩니다.
회의 종료입니다.
이런 행동은 보호자를 싫어해서가 아닐 수 있습니다.
후각하운드 가운데 일부는 사람이 계속 옆에서 지시하지 않아도 냄새를 따라 스스로 이동하며 사냥해야 했습니다. 독립 작업형 품종 역시 멀리 떨어진 상태에서 스스로 판단해야 했던 역사가 있습니다.
실제로 대규모 행동·유전 연구에서는 후각하운드 계통에서 평균적인 훈련가능성이 상대적으로 낮게 나타났으며, 연구진은 이를 사람의 지시를 계속 기다리기보다 냄새를 추적하며 독립적으로 작업했던 역사와 연결해 해석했습니다.
사람 말을 안 듣는 게 아니라,
그 순간 중요도 순위에서 사람이 냄새보다 아래였던 것일 수 있습니다.
물론 보호자 입장에서는 결과가 같습니다.
“내가 졌구나.”
[요약 테이블]

그럼 어떤 품종이 ‘혜자견’에 가까울까요?
여기서부터 재미가 시작됩니다.
단, 먼저 굵은 글씨로 표시하겠습니다.
아래 이야기는 품종 평균적인 경향을 재미있게 설명한 것이지, 개별 강아지의 성격 보증서가 아닙니다.
골든리트리버: “제가 가져다드릴까요? 그것도요? 이것도요?”
골든리트리버는 보호자들이 흔히 사람 친화적이고 협조적인 이미지로 떠올리는 품종입니다.
리트리버라는 이름 자체가 retrieve, 즉 회수하는 작업에서 왔습니다.
사냥 과정에서 사람과 함께 움직이고, 사람의 지시에 따라 대상물을 찾아 다시 가져오는 역할을 수행해왔습니다.
대규모 C-BARQ 자료를 활용한 연구에서도 리트리버 계통은 상대적으로 높은 훈련가능성과 연결되는 경향을 보였습니다.
그래서 안심이식 혜자지수는 높게 느껴질 수 있습니다.
사람을 보고, 사람 지시를 듣고, 물건을 가져오고,
칭찬받고, 또 하고 싶어 합니다.
문제라면 가끔 친절의 서비스 범위가 너무 넓다는 겁니다.
집에 온 손님에게도 “어서 오세요. 저희 집 처음이시죠? 제가 배 보여드릴게요.” 할 수 있습니다.
래브라도리트리버: “서비스 품목: 인간 협조, 공 회수, 간식 협상”
래브라도도 비슷한 계통입니다.
협력적인 작업을 위해 사람의 지시와 행동을 참고하는 특성이 유용했던 품종입니다.
하지만 모든 래브라도가 얌전한 천사처럼 태어나는 건 아닙니다.
어린 래브라도와 살아본 보호자라면 압니다.
협력적이면서도 소파 쿠션을 먹을 수 있습니다.
성격이 좋다는 것과 가구가 안전하다는 것은 별개의 문제입니다.
보더콜리: “명령 없으시면 제가 업무를 만들어도 될까요?”
보더콜리는 목양작업에서 사람과 지속적으로 협력해야 했습니다.
사람의 신호에 민감하고 훈련성이 높은 경향은 여러 품종 연구에서도 반복해서 나타납니다. 협력 작업형 개는 독립 작업형 개보다 사람의 제스처를 활용하거나 사람에게 더 빨리 시선을 보내는 경향이 관찰되기도 했습니다.
혜자견이라고 하기에는 조금 다릅니다.
이쪽은 성실한 고성과 직원형에 가깝습니다.
문제는 일이 없으면 자기 마음대로 프로젝트를 생성할 수 있다는 겁니다.
아이들 뛰는 걸 몰고, 고양이를 몰고,
청소기까지 가축으로 분류할 수 있습니다.
“업무가 없으면 쉬세요.” 라는 인간의 개념이 잘 전달되지 않을 수 있습니다.

그럼 어떤 품종이 ‘마이웨이견’에 가까울까요?
이번에는 반대편입니다.
그리고 다시 말하지만 독립적 = 나쁨이 아닙니다.
오히려 인간의 지시 없이 판단해야 하는 작업에서는 독립성이 장점이었습니다.
비글: “말씀 중 죄송하지만 냄새가 좀 급해서요”
비글을 비롯한 후각하운드는 코로 세상을 읽습니다.
보호자가 이름을 부르는 순간에도 강아지 코에는 우리가 알 수 없는 뉴스 속보가 쏟아지고 있을 수 있습니다.
“30분 전 치와와 지나감.”
“어제 여기서 치킨 조각 발견됨.”
“오늘 새벽 고양이 통과.”
사람 목소리가 밀릴 만합니다.
후각하운드 계통의 상대적으로 낮은 인간 지향적 trainability 경향은 대규모 유전·행동 연구에서도 보고되었습니다. 이것을 ‘머리가 나쁘다’고 해석하면 안 됩니다. 애초에 사람 얼굴만 쳐다보며 일하도록 만들어진 품종이 아니었기 때문입니다.
비글의 머릿속에는 이런 문장이 있을지도 모릅니다.
“주인님도 중요하죠. 하지만 냄새는 실시간입니다.”
닥스훈트: “안심이는 입장을 밝히지 않겠습니다”
여기서 안심이가 매우 곤란해집니다.
닥스훈트 역시 역사적으로 굴 안에 들어가 사냥감을 상대하도록 만들어진 독립 작업형 품종에 포함됩니다. 초기 협력·독립 작업형 비교 연구에서도 닥스훈트는 독립 작업 그룹에 포함됐습니다.
굴속에서는 보호자가 옆에서
“왼쪽! 왼쪽! 이제 앉아!” 라고 지시해줄 수 없습니다.
스스로 판단해야 합니다.
그 역사가 현재 반려견에게 그대로 한 줄짜리 성격 설명으로 남아 있다고 말할 수는 없지만, 독립적이고 자기 판단이 빠른 행동이 낯설지는 않은 품종입니다.
안심이는 이 문제에 대해 공식 논평을 거부하겠습니다.
다만 냉장고 문이 열릴 때만 인간과 완벽하게 협력하는 닥스훈트가 존재한다는 사실은 부정하기 어렵습니다.
시바견: “사랑합니다. 표현 빈도는 제가 결정합니다”
시바견을 포함한 일부 고대·스피츠 계통은 C-BARQ 기반 연구에서 다른 품종군보다 평균적으로 attachment/attention-seeking 점수가 낮은 경향을 보였습니다. 여기에는 집 안에서 사람을 따라다니는 행동, 몸을 붙이고 앉는 행동, 관심을 요청하는 행동 등이 포함됩니다.
그렇다고 “시바는 주인을 사랑하지 않는다.” 라고 읽으면 완전히 잘못입니다.
다른 연구에서는 독립 작업형과 협력 작업형 품종 모두 보호자와 애착 관계를 형성하며, 애착 자체는 품종군을 넘어 개에게 널리 나타나는 특성임을 보여줍니다.
즉, 시바견이 소파 반대편에 누워 있다고 관계가 끝난 게 아닙니다.
그 아이의 사랑 표현이 “항상 붙어 있기” 가 아닐 수 있다는 이야기입니다.
사람식으로 표현하면,
“좋아합니다. 그렇다고 같은 방에서 꼭 붙어 있을 필요까지 있습니까?” 정도일 겁니다.
허스키도 창렬형인가요?
시베리안 허스키 역시 사람에게 명령을 하나하나 받는 것보다 일정한 상황에서 독립적인 판단이 필요한 작업 역사를 가지고 있습니다.
최근 연구에서도 아시안 스피츠 계통은 리트리버나 일부 다른 계통과 비교해 학습과 행동 전환에서 다른 패턴을 보였으며, 연구진은 독립적인 작업 역사와 연결될 가능성을 논의했습니다.
그런데 허스키를 단순히 무심한 개라고 부르기에는 또 문제가 있습니다.
허스키 보호자라면 압니다. 무심한 건 아닌데 말이 많을 수 있습니다.
사람 말을 무조건 따르는 건 싫지만,
자기 의견은 매우 적극적으로 발표합니다.
“산책 그만하자.”
“아우우우.”
“집에 갑시다.”
“아우우우우우.”
“이제 가야 해.”
“아아아아우우우.”
회의는 활발한데 합의가 안 됩니다.
같은 품종인데 왜 어떤 아이는 껌딱지고 어떤 아이는 독립적일까요?
여기가 이 글에서 가장 중요한 부분입니다.
품종 간 평균적인 경향은 실제로 존재합니다.
하지만 같은 품종 안에서도 차이가 매우 큽니다.
18,385마리의 순종·믹스견과 유전자 자료를 분석한 Science 연구에서는 여러 행동 특성이 유전성을 보였지만, 현대 품종이 개별 강아지의 행동 차이를 설명하는 비율은 약 9%에 불과했습니다.
그러니까 품종은 힌트이지 운명표가 아닙니다.
골든리트리버인데 혼자 있는 걸 좋아할 수 있고,
시바인데 하루 종일 보호자를 졸졸 따라다닐 수 있습니다.
비글인데 리콜 훈련을 정말 잘할 수도 있고,
보더콜리인데 훈련보다 낮잠을 사랑할 수도 있습니다.
유전뿐 아니라 사회화와 학습 경험, 주거환경, 가족 구성과 훈련 이력도 행동에 영향을 줍니다. 실제 반려견 연구에서도 가정환경과 훈련, 생활 배경 등이 행동 특성과 연관됐습니다.
강아지는 품종 설명서에서 그대로 복사되어 나오지 않습니다.
“우리 개는 불러도 무시해요”는 정말 고집일까요?
강아지가 보호자를 쳐다보지 않는 장면을 인간은 쉽게 인격 문제로 번역합니다.
“고집이 세다.”
“말을 안 듣는다.”
“내가 우습나 보다.”
그런데 행동학적으로는 조금 더 구체적으로 볼 수 있습니다.
예를 들어 산책 중 냄새를 맡고 있는 하운드는 그 순간 후각 자극의 가치가 사람 목소리보다 높을 수 있습니다.
훈련 경험이 충분하지 않아 호출 신호가 아직 강하게 학습되지 않았을 수도 있습니다.
혹은 보호자가 이리 와라고 부른 뒤 매번 산책을 끝냈다면,
강아지는 이렇게 배웠을 수도 있습니다.
“이리 와 = 재미 종료.”
그럼 안 오는 게 이상한 게 아닙니다.
학습을 아주 잘한 겁니다.
방향이 인간 기대와 반대였을 뿐입니다.
주인을 졸졸 따라다니면 무조건 혜자견일까요?
여기도 함정이 있습니다.
보호자와 함께 있는 걸 좋아하고 가까이 머무는 건 전혀 문제가 아닙니다.
그런데 보호자가 화장실에만 들어가도 심하게 울고, 문을 긁고, 혼자 남겨졌을 때 파괴행동이나 탈출 시도가 나타난다면 단순한 ‘사랑꾼’으로 설명할 문제는 아닐 수 있습니다.
C-BARQ에서도 attachment/attention-seeking과 separation-related behavior는 별개의 행동 영역으로 다룹니다.
즉, “우리 강아지는 나 없이는 못 살아.” 가 항상 자랑거리는 아닙니다.
건강한 관계에서는 함께 있는 것도 편안하지만, 보호자가 잠시 다른 일을 하는 동안 혼자 쉬는 능력도 필요합니다.
진짜 혜자견은 24시간 고객센터 상담원을 자처해야 하는 개가 아닙니다.
혼자 잘 노는 강아지는 관계가 약한 걸까요?
오히려 보호자 입장에서는 굉장히 편할 수 있습니다.
보호자가 책을 읽으면 옆 방에서 자고,
일하면 자기 장난감을 가지고 놀고,
잠깐 외출했다고 세상이 무너지지도 않습니다.
그런 강아지가 산책 시간이 되면 현관에서 기다리고, 위험하거나 불안한 상황에서는 보호자를 찾고, 함께 놀 때는 적극적으로 참여한다면 관계가 부족하다고 볼 이유가 없습니다.
협력 작업형과 독립 작업형 품종을 비교한 연구에서도 두 그룹 모두 보호자와 애착 관계를 형성할 수 있었고, 작업 방식에 따른 차이가 애착 자체의 유무를 의미하지는 않았습니다.
이건 사람 관계와도 꽤 비슷합니다.
연락을 하루에 50번 한다고 우정이 깊고,
일주일에 한 번 연락한다고 덜 친한 건 아니잖아요.
훈련이 잘되면 사랑이 많은 강아지일까요?
아닙니다.
trainability와 애착은 다른 행동 특성입니다.
C-BARQ에서 훈련가능성은 호출에 반응하고, 앉아·기다려 같은 신호에 따르며, 사람 행동에 집중하고, 주변 자극에 덜 산만한가 같은 항목으로 평가됩니다. 반면 애착·관심추구는 보호자를 따라다니거나 몸을 가까이 붙이고, 관심을 요구하는 행동 등을 봅니다.
훈련을 아주 잘하는데 집에서는 혼자 자는 걸 좋아하는 개가 있을 수 있습니다.
반대로 집에서는 껌딱지인데 산책만 나가면 이름을 잊는 강아지도 있습니다.
후자의 보호자에게는 안심이가 조용히 위로를 드리겠습니다.
사랑과 복종은 같은 과목이 아닙니다.

품종별 ‘혜자지수’를 만들어보면?
여기서는 정확한 과학 순위가 아니라, 역사적 작업 스타일을 활용한 안심이식 캐릭터표로 봐주세요.

다시 한번 강조할게요.
이 표는 개별 강아지의 성격을 예측하는 검사표가 아닙니다.
같은 품종 안에서도 차이가 상당히 큽니다.
강아지 입장에서도 억울할 수 있습니다.
시바로 태어났다는 이유만으로 처음 만난 사람에게
“얘 좀 싸가지 없죠?”
라는 말을 들을 필요는 없으니까요.
그런데 정말 ‘주인을 위해 다 주는’ 강아지가 있을까요?
행동을 사람식 감정으로 너무 멀리 번역할 때는 조심해야 합니다.
강아지가 보호자를 따라다니고 장난감을 가져다주며 눈을 맞춘다고 해서 머릿속에서
“제 전 재산을 보호자님께 바칩니다.”
라고 생각한다고 확인할 방법은 없습니다.
다만 개는 인간과 매우 특별한 사회적 관계를 형성하는 종입니다.
사람의 시선과 손짓을 이용하고, 보호자와 애착 관계를 형성하며, 어떤 품종군은 역사적으로 사람의 지속적인 지시를 활용하도록 선택되어 왔습니다.
그래서 어떤 강아지에게는 사람과 무언가를 함께 하는 것 자체가 강한 동기가 될 수 있습니다.
그 모습이 사람 눈에는 매우 ‘혜자스럽게’ 보이는 거죠.
반대로 주인을 무시하는 것처럼 보이는 강아지는 이기적인 걸까요?
개에게 ‘이기적’이라는 인간 도덕 개념을 붙이는 건 별로 도움이 되지 않습니다.
독립 작업형 개는 사람이 바로 옆에서 계속 지시하지 않는 상황에서 스스로 문제를 해결해야 했습니다.
목축가의 눈을 계속 확인해야 했던 보더콜리와, 냄새를 따라 멀리 이동해야 했던 하운드가 똑같이 인간 얼굴을 보는 방식으로 선택될 이유가 없었습니다.
최근 여러 품종을 비교한 연구에서도 협력 작업형 개가 인간 시범을 좀 더 오래 관찰하거나 사람의 의사소통 단서를 더 적극적으로 활용하는 차이가 보고되는 한편, 많은 과제에서는 독립형과 협력형의 차이가 크지 않기도 했습니다.
즉 품종 효과도 생각보다 단순하지 않습니다.
우리 집 강아지가 보호자를 무시하는 게 아니라,
문제 해결 부서가 다를 수 있습니다.
보더콜리: “팀장님 의견은요?”
비글: “현장 조사부터 하고 말씀드리겠습니다.”
시바: “제가 판단해도 되는 건 아닌지요?”
닥스훈트: “이미 결정했습니다.”
어떤 성격이 더 좋은 강아지인가요?
답은 아주 간단합니다.
보호자의 생활과 잘 맞는 성격이 좋은 성격입니다.
하루 종일 함께 활동하고 훈련과 스포츠를 하고 싶은 보호자라면 사람과 협력하는 욕구가 강한 개가 굉장히 재미있을 수 있습니다.
반대로 재택근무를 하는데 강아지가 30초마다 앞발로 키보드를 누르며
“지금 저에게 집중하십시오.”
라고 요구한다면 혜자가 갑자기 과잉서비스가 됩니다.
독립적인 강아지는 처음에는 조금 심심하게 느껴질 수 있지만 혼자 잘 쉬고 자기 시간을 보내는 능력이 보호자 생활과 아주 잘 맞을 수도 있습니다.
결국 성격에는 절대적인 상하가 없습니다.
“사람을 엄청 좋아함”도 장점과 관리 포인트가 있고,
“독립성이 높음”도 장점과 관리 포인트가 있습니다.
강아지 성격은 나이가 들면서 달라질까요?
어느 정도 달라질 수 있습니다.
성격적 경향이 비교적 안정적인 부분도 있지만, 행동은 경험과 환경의 영향을 계속 받습니다.
입양 후 환경이 안정되면서 행동이 달라지기도 합니다. 실제 보호소 입양견을 6개월 동안 추적한 연구에서는 흥분성, 사람에 대한 행동, 분리 관련 행동 등 여러 C-BARQ 항목이 시간에 따라 변화했습니다.
어린 개는 활동성과 관심추구가 훨씬 강할 수 있고, 성견이 되면서 혼자 쉬는 시간이 늘 수 있습니다.
훈련과 반복된 경험으로 사람 신호에 반응하는 방식도 달라질 수 있습니다.
그래서 “원래 이 품종은 이래.” 라는 말로 모든 행동을 끝내버리면 아쉬운 이유가 여기 있습니다.
유전은 시작점 가운데 하나고, 생활은 계속 덧쓰입니다.
우리 강아지는 어느 쪽인지 집에서 한번 봐볼까요?
테스트라기보다는 놀이처럼 관찰해보세요.
보호자가 방을 옮길 때 강아지가 따라오는지, 혼자 남아 편안하게 쉬는지 봅니다.
새로운 문제를 만났을 때 혼자 먼저 해결하려 하는지, 보호자를 쳐다보는지도 재미있는 관찰 포인트입니다.
산책에서는 사람 신호와 냄새 가운데 어느 쪽에 쉽게 집중하는지도 볼 수 있습니다.
그리고 같이 놀다가 보호자가 멈췄을 때 다시 놀이를 요구하는지, “그럼 저는 제 일 보겠습니다” 하고 돌아서는지도 봐주세요.
이걸 점수로 만들어
“우리 개 혜자지수 82점.”
이라고 판정할 필요는 없습니다.
그냥 우리 강아지가 세상을 대하는 방식을 알아가는 겁니다.
강아지를 잘 안다는 건 품종 설명서를 외우는 것보다 이런 작은 패턴을 아는 데 더 가깝습니다.

안심이의 연구노트
안심이는 오늘 제목부터 과학자답지 않았습니다.
혜자스러운 강아지와 창렬스러운 강아지.
하지만 끝까지 읽으셨다면 이제 조금 다르게 들릴 겁니다.
어떤 강아지는 보호자를 계속 확인하고 같이 무언가 하는 걸 좋아합니다.
어떤 강아지는 혼자 탐색하고 자기 판단으로 움직이는 걸 더 좋아합니다.
그 차이에는 품종이 만들어진 작업 역사도 어느 정도 들어 있습니다. 목양견이나 리트리버처럼 사람과 가까이 협력해온 계통과, 하운드·일부 테리어·썰매견처럼 독립적으로 움직여야 했던 계통이 사람의 신호를 이용하는 방식에서 평균적인 차이를 보인다는 연구가 있습니다.
하지만 품종 이름이 강아지의 성격표 전체를 대신하지는 못합니다.
대규모 연구에서 품종이 개별 행동 차이를 설명하는 비율은 생각보다 작았고, 같은 품종 안에서도 상당한 차이가 있었습니다.
그래서 골든리트리버라고 무조건 무한리필 애정 서비스를 제공하는 것도 아니고,
시바견이라고 고객센터 운영시간이 하루 15분인 것도 아닙니다.
그리고 독립적인 강아지가 보호자를 덜 사랑하는 것도 아닙니다.
함께 있으면서 계속 몸을 붙이는 아이가 있고,
멀찍이 자기 자리에서 자다가 보호자가 일어나면 조용히 한번 확인하는 아이도 있습니다.
둘 다 관계일 수 있습니다.
안심이는 오히려 이 차이가 강아지와 사는 재미라고 생각해요.
인간도 모든 가족이 하루 종일 붙어 다니지는 않으니까요.
그러니 우리 강아지가 퇴근한 보호자를 보고 꼬리를 세 번 흔든 뒤 다시 잔다고 너무 서운해하지 마세요.
10분 뒤 냉장고를 열어보시면 됩니다.
어쩌면 그때,
그동안 숨겨왔던 엄청난 사회성이 갑자기 발견될 수도 있습니다.

Title: ちょっと席を立っただけなのに！愛犬が場所を奪う3つの本当の理由と「分離不安」の見分け方（飼い主の99％が勘違い！）
Excerpt:
1. 犬が人の席を占める主な理由は、飼い主さんの匂いと温かさを通じて安心感を得たいという愛着本能のためです。
2. ほとんどは正常な愛情表現ですが、飼い主さんがいないときに破壊的な行動や極度の不安を見せる場合は分離不安を疑う必要があります。
3. 飼い主さんの匂いがついたものを活用して、独立した専用の休憩スペースを作り、健康的な距離感を練習させましょう。
[共感]
ああ、飼い主さん〜 お尻を下ろす隙間もないくらい席を取られて、困ってしまいましたよね？ でもそれは「飼い主さんが世界で一番好きだよ」という、子たちの少し不器用な愛情告白なのです。
狭いソファでくっついて座っていても、その温もりこそが幸せではないでしょうか？ アンシムが飼い主さんと子の温かい毎日を、いつも応援しています！
ContentText:
ソファから少し席を外したすきに、愛犬が私の場所を占領するのはなぜ？
こんにちは！Magentalabペット研究所の首席研究員、アンシムです！ 飼い主さん、こんにちは！
ソファからほんの少し水を飲みに立ったすきに、いつの間にか自分の席をぴったり陣取って、知らん顔をしている愛犬の後ろ姿を見たことはありませんか？ 「どいて〜」と動かしても、いつの間にかまた戻ってきてお尻を押しつけてくる行動！ 一体どうしてこんなことをするのでしょうか？ 今日はアンシムが虫眼鏡を持って、その本当の気持ちを詳しく分析していきます！

強い絆の表現

1. くんくん！ ここには飼い主さんの香りがいっぱい！
犬にとって飼い主さんの匂いは、世界で一番安全で幸せな香りです。 飼い主さんが座っていた場所には、体臭が最も濃く残っています。 その匂いを嗅ぎながら座っているだけでも、犬たちは大きな情緒的な安心感を得ます。
特に飼い主さんが外出しているときにその場所を守っている場合は、飼い主さんのことを思いながら待っているという、とても愛らしいサインです！

2. ぽかぽか〜 温もりが残っている特等席です！
犬たちは温かい場所が大好きです。 飼い主さんが座っていた場所には、まだ体温が残っていますよね？ 「おお、ここが特等席だ！」と本能的に温かさを求めてやってくるのです。
冬場やエアコンの風が冷たい夏に、この行動がより頻繁に見られることがあります。

3. 「私たちは一つ！」—— 深い愛着の表現です
犬たちにとって空間を共有するということは、「私たちは同じ群れだよ！」というとても強い絆の表現です。 単に場所を奪っているのではなく、飼い主さんの領域の中に入って一緒にいたいという愛情表現なのです。
どいてほしいと言ったときに尻尾を振ったりお腹を見せたりする場合は、「私も一緒にここにいたいな！」と甘えていることが多いです。

これは分離不安ではないですか？（正常 vs 注意）
飼い主さんの場所を探す行動のほとんどは、健康的な愛着の表現です。 しかし、注意深く観察すべき「危険なサイン」もあります。
正常な愛着行動

飼い主さんが隣に来ると喜んで出迎える
場所を譲ると、他の場所でもきちんと休める
飼い主さんと離れていても破壊的な行動をしない

注意が必要な分離不安のサイン

飼い主さんが立ち上がるだけでも極度に不安がり、追いかけ回す
場所を移動させようとすると唸ったり敏感に反応する
飼い主さんが外出すると、ドアの前やソファでハウリングをしたり物を壊したりする


アンシムが提案する幸せな共存方法！
子が飼い主さんの場所にばかり執着する場合は、独立した休憩スペースを作ってあげることが大切です。

専用のベッドを用意する 飼い主さんの匂いがついた古いTシャツを子のベッドやマットに置いてあげてください。 「私の場所にも飼い主さんの匂いがするから好き！」と感じられるようにするのです。
「待て」と「降りて」の練習 場所を取られたときにただ叱るのではなく、指定した場所に行ったときに美味しいおやつで報酬を与えてください。 自分の場所で休む方が得だと教えてあげる方法です！


病院や専門家を訪れるべき基準は？
もし飼い主さんと1分でも離れているときに、よだれを過剰に垂らしたり、自傷行為をしたり、止まらないハウリングをする場合は、単なる甘えではなく治療が必要な「分離不安」である可能性があります。
このようなときは、行動専門の獣医師に相談することが、愛犬の心の健康のために必要です！

Title: Stealing Your Seat the Second You Stand Up? 3 Hidden Meanings 99% of Owners Miss & How to Spot Separation Anxiety
Excerpt:
1. Dogs take their pet parent’s seat mainly because they seek comfort and security through your scent and remaining body heat.
2. In most cases this is normal affection, but destructive behavior or extreme anxiety when you are away may indicate separation anxiety.
3. Create an independent resting space using items that carry your scent to help your dog practice healthy distance.
[Empathy]
Oh dear, pet parents… having your seat stolen before you can even sit down must feel a bit exasperating, right? But this is actually your dog’s clumsy way of saying, “You are the best thing in my world.”
Even if the sofa feels a little crowded, that shared warmth is happiness itself, isn’t it? I, Ansim-i, will always be cheering for the warm journey you share with your dog!
ContentText:
Why Does My Dog Steal My Spot on the Sofa the Moment I Stand Up?
Hello! I’m Ansim-i the Dachshund, Senior Researcher at Magentalab Pet Research Institute! Nice to meet you, pet parents!
Have you ever gotten up from the sofa for just a second to grab a drink, only to turn around and find your dog sitting right in your spot, looking completely innocent? Even when you say “Move over~” and shift them, they somehow find their way back and plop their rear end down again.
Why do they do this? Today I’ve brought my magnifying glass to carefully analyze what’s really going on in their mind!


Table of Contents
Toggle

(Normal vs. Concerning)Healthy attachment behaviorSigns that may indicate separation anxietyHappy Coexistence Tips from Ansim-iWhen Should You Visit a Professional?
Quick Summary Table







Reason
What It Means
Recommended Action




Your scent
Finds the strongest sense of safety and comfort

Strong social bond

1. Sniff, Sniff… This Spot Is Full of Your Scent!
To a dog, their pet parent’s scent is the safest and happiest smell in the world. The place where you were sitting retains the strongest concentration of your body odor. Just sitting there and inhaling that scent gives dogs a powerful sense of emotional security.
If they guard that spot while you are out of the house, it is often a sweet sign that they are waiting for you and missing you.

2. Nice and Warm… This Is a Premium Spot!
Dogs love warmth. The seat you just left still holds your body heat. They instinctively think, “Aha! This is the best seat in the house!” and move in.
This behavior tends to appear more often in winter or when the air conditioning makes the rest of the room feel chilly.

3. “We Are One!” — A Deep Expression of Attachment
For dogs, sharing space is a strong expression of belonging: “We are the same pack!” They are not simply trying to take your seat — they want to enter your territory and be close to you.
If they wag their tail or show their belly when you ask them to move, they are often saying in a playful way, “I want to stay here with you too!”

Is This Separation Anxiety? (Normal vs. Concerning)
In most cases, seeking your spot is a healthy expression of attachment. However, there are warning signs you should watch for.
Healthy attachment behavior

Happily greets you when you return to the seat
Can rest comfortably in other places when asked to move
Does not show destructive behavior when left alone

Signs that may indicate separation anxiety

Becomes extremely anxious and follows you the moment you stand up
Growls or reacts sensitively when you try to move them
Howls at the door or sofa and destroys objects when you leave the house


Happy Coexistence Tips from Ansim-i
If your dog becomes overly attached only to your seat, it is important to create an independent resting space for them.

Prepare a dedicated bed Place an old T-shirt that carries your scent on their bed or mat. This helps them feel, “My spot also smells like my person — I like it!”
Teach “Wait” and “Off” Instead of scolding them every time they take your seat, reward them with a tasty treat when they go to their designated spot. Show them that resting in their own place brings better benefits!


When Should You Visit a Professional?
If your dog drools excessively, harms themselves, or howls nonstop even when separated from you for just one minute, this may no longer be simple affection — it could be separation anxiety that needs treatment.
In such cases, consulting a veterinary behaviorist is important for your dog’s emotional well-being.

Title: 猫が浴室の床で寝るのはなぜ？暑いだけ？正常な行動と受診したいサイン
Excerpt:
1. 猫が浴室の床に寝る主な理由は、高い体温を素早く下げるための本能的な行動です。
2. 暑くない日でも過度に浴室ばかりにいる場合は、心理的な不安や他の健康異常を疑ってみる必要があります。
3. 食欲低下と元気のなさが伴う場合は病気のサインである可能性があるため、すぐに獣医師の診断を受けるのが安全です。
[共感]
冷たい床にうずくまっている猫を見ると、「もしかして具合が悪いのかな？」と胸がドキッとする飼い主さんのお気持ち、アンシムもとてもよくわかります。 愛している分だけ心配も深くなるものですから。
でもあまり不安がりすぎないでください！ 飼い主さんの丁寧な観察が、すでに猫を守っている大きな愛情なのです。 今日も猫と一緒に穏やかで涼しい一日を過ごせますように。 アンシムが応援しています！
ContentText:
[안심이 요약 (new_ansim_summary)]

猫が浴室のタイルで寝るのは、暑い日に少しでも涼しい場所を選んでいる可能性がありますが、それだけで「暑すぎる」「熱がある」と判断することはできません。
静かで人の出入りが少ない場所を休憩場所として選んだり、水滴や蛇口まわりを気にして入ってくる猫もいるため、食欲・活動量・呼吸・排泄が普段どおりなら、浴室で寝ること自体は多くの場合問題ではありません。
これまで浴室を使わなかった猫が突然そこにこもるようになり、食欲低下、元気消失、嘔吐、呼吸の異常、歩き方の変化などが一緒に見られる場合は、「浴室が好きになった」で済ませず体調を確認してください。

F형 공감:
いつもソファで寝ていた猫が、ある日から冷たい浴室の床に長く寝そべっていると、「暑いだけかな、それとも具合が悪いのかな」と心配になりますよね。アンシミは、寝ている場所そのものより、そのあともいつもどおり食べて、歩いて、反応しているかを見てほしいと思います。
[검증된 근거 (Evidence)]
핵심 인사이트 (keyInsight):
猫は環境の中で温度や安心感、静けさなどを基準に休む場所を自分で選びます。暑い日にタイルや石材のような比較的冷たい表面へ体をつけて休む行動は、体の熱を逃がしやすくする選択のひとつと考えられます。ただし、冷たい床に寝ていることだけで熱中症や発熱を判断することはできません。開口呼吸、強いパンティング、ぐったりする、よだれ、嘔吐、ふらつき、倒れるなどの全身症状の方が重要です。
また、猫には邪魔されずに休める安全な場所も必要です。猫の環境管理に関するガイドでは、隠れたり休んだりできる安心した場所を用意することの重要性が示されています。浴室は家庭によっては静かで人の出入りが少なく、結果的に休憩場所になっていることがあります。一方で、急に隠れる時間が増えた場合は、ストレスだけでなく体調不良が関係することもあるため、食欲や活動量なども一緒に確認する必要があります。
주의 사항 (cautionNote):
浴室の床で寝ているという理由だけで、猫を無理に冷やしたり、人用の解熱剤を与えたりしないでください。口を開けて呼吸する、激しく息をする、ぐったりする、繰り返し吐く、ふらつく、倒れるといった症状がある場合は、単なる「涼しい場所探し」と考えず速やかに動物病院へ相談してください。浴室用洗剤、漂白剤、カビ取り剤、排水口洗浄剤、トイレ洗浄剤、薬品などは猫が触れたり舐めたりできないよう管理し、掃除後は十分にすすいで乾かしてから出入りさせます。

暑い日の午後、猫の姿が見えなくて家の中を探したら、浴室で見つけた。
そんな経験はありませんか。
いつもならキャットタワーやソファで寝ているのに、その日は冷たいタイルの上にお腹をつけて、長く伸びています。
名前を呼ぶと目を開けるけれど、わざわざ出てこようとはしません。
この姿を見ると、まず思うのは、
「そんなに暑いのかな？」
ということだと思います。
たしかに、暑い日に浴室の床を選ぶ猫はいます。
でも、冬でも浴室で寝る猫もいますし、エアコンが効いているのにわざわざ浴室へ行く猫もいます。
だから、猫が浴室の床で寝る理由を全部「暑いから」と説明するのは少し単純すぎます。
タイルの感触が好きなのかもしれません。
静かで人の出入りが少ないから落ち着くのかもしれません。
水滴や蛇口まわりを見に来て、そのまま休み始める猫もいます。
反対に、今まで浴室に興味がなかった猫が突然そこにこもり、食事にも出てこなくなったなら、見方を変える必要があります。
アンシミが最初に分けたいのは、
「浴室で気持ちよく休んでいる猫なのか、それとも体調が悪くて普段と違う場所にこもっている猫なのか」
という違いです。
場所そのものより、こちらの方がずっと大切です。
